title: New APs fail to join after a controller replacement
scenario: A site replaced controller 10.10.0.5 with 10.10.50.5. Existing APs were manually pointed to the replacement, but newly installed, unprimed APs fail to join. Routing, AP/controller software compatibility and permitted CAPWAP connectivity to 10.10.50.5 have been independently verified. The following records are representative.

exhibits.title: R1 DHCP pool excerpt
exhibits.text:
ip dhcp pool AP-MGMT
 network 10.10.60.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 10.10.60.1
 option 43 hex f104.0a0a.0005

exhibits.title: New AP discovery observation
exhibits.text:
Lease: 10.10.60.101/24; gateway 10.10.60.1
Received option 43 controller candidate: 10.10.0.5
No stored controller and no controller DNS record
Requests sent to 10.10.0.5; no response
Retired controller 10.10.0.5 is powered off

question: Which fault is directly supported by the records?
options: The new APs received a valid address but obsolete controller-discovery information
The replacement controller has no return route to the new AP subnet
The new AP image is incompatible with the replacement controller
A CAPWAP control filter blocks the replacement controller's responses
explanation: The option-43 address decodes to the retired 10.10.0.5, and the AP observation confirms that it used that candidate. CAPWAP can cross routed subnets; the independently verified new-controller path should be used after discovery is corrected.
fix:
In the isolated lab, change only this pool's option, then have one test AP reacquire its DHCP discovery information using that platform's supported renewal/restart procedure. Do not clear every network lease.

```ios
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool AP-MGMT
R1(dhcp-config)# no option 43
R1(dhcp-config)# option 43 hex f104.0a0a.3205
R1(dhcp-config)# end
```

Confirm the next DHCP information names 10.10.50.5, then confirm discovery responses and actual AP registration. A successful ping alone does not prove the join.

title: The branch AP is joined, but local guests cannot get a lease
scenario: A FlexConnect AP sends management untagged in VLAN 10. CORP is centrally switched and works. GUEST is explicitly configured for local switching with tagged VLAN 30. VLAN 30, its gateway, DHCP pool and upstream trunk have been verified using a wired test client. Records below are representative.

exhibits.title: SW1 AP-facing port
exhibits.text:
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/7
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 spanning-tree portfast

exhibits.title: AP/WLAN and wired test
exhibits.text:
AP management: 10.10.0.51/24; controller state joined
GUEST: local switching, VLAN 30, security completed
Wireless GUEST client: no lease
Wired test in VLAN 30: 10.30.0.101/24, gateway 10.30.0.1; reachable

question: Which mismatch explains the guest failure?
options: The AP's local client VLAN is missing from its Ethernet port contract
The guest gateway rejects every DHCP request from a wired client
The controller's central CORP mapping prevents AP registration
The GUEST security exchange fails before the client may request addressing
explanation: The access port carries untagged VLAN 10 but does not match the AP's required tagged local guest VLAN. Management and the centrally switched CORP WLAN can work while this separate local forwarding path fails.
fix:
In the authorized lab, change the AP port to the documented trunk contract:

```ios
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/7
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk native vlan 10
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,30
SW1(config-if)# spanning-tree portfast trunk
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show interfaces trunk
```

Allow any link/control reconvergence, confirm AP registration, and request a fresh guest lease. Verify a 10.30.0.x/24 address, gateway 10.30.0.1 and actual guest access; then retest CORP.
